explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LN RS (GPT-4-based metric) with human evaluation rankings across three base models (LLAMA2-7B, LLAMA2-13B, PYTHIA-6.9B) on a shared set of 192 data points, showing similar preference patterns where preference-optimized models are ranked highest by both humans and LN RS

prompts.notes: Paper mentions prompt template is provided in Appendix A but this appendix is not included in the provided text; also mentions order reversal technique to reduce position bias

guidelines.notes: Detailed instructions provided in Appendix B (not included in text); human evaluators ranked responses based on Overall Appropriateness, Social Understanding, and Conversational Insightfulness

sample_size.notes: All 192 data points were evaluated by both GPT-4 (LN RS) and human evaluators; each human evaluator assessed 16 data points

quantitative_scores.notes: Paper reports qualitative alignment between LN RS trends and human rankings but does not provide a specific correlation coefficient value or statistical significance testing

validation_results.summary_finding: LN RS metric based on GPT-4 judgments shows alignment with human preferences, consistently ranking preference-optimized models highest across all tested LLMs, though no quantitative correlation coefficient is reported

llm_only_criteria: LN RS (quality relative to gold answer)
criteria_mapping.notes: GPT-4 evaluates responses relative to gold answers using LN RS, while humans rank responses based on specific pragmatic criteria; both evaluate the same underlying pragmatic quality dimensions
